name: Irina → Liza-style

measuredVoice.character: young, warm-bright, calm, friendly, connected Russian explainer delivery

targetStyle.goal: Bring Irina closer to Liza's warm, youthful delivery while preserving Irina's identity and Russian clarity.
targetStyle.endingStyle: soften final 35-70 ms of spoken phrases; use 18-25 ms fade-in after pauses; avoid hard digital silence

mastering.compression: very gentle, ratio about 1.35:1, slower attack and release

videoStyle.master: 16:9, 30fps H.264; 1280x720 acceptable for 10-second free previews, 1920x1080 for clean master
videoStyle.presenter: Liza on the left, persistent identity
videoStyle.background: dark navy/black technology UI with subtle grid and cyan accents
videoStyle.layout: presenter left; headline/idea center; cards, diagrams or waveform right
videoStyle.motion: restrained fade/slide/scale/line-draw, no random camera movement
videoStyle.audioOrder: voice first, match reference micro-pauses, then subtle ambience/SFX

freePipeline.postProcess: phrase-boundary microfades + short room tone + FFmpeg rubberband formant-preserved pitch + warm EQ + gentle de-ess/compression + loudness match

rules: Do not claim Irina is the exact Liza voice; this is a prosody/style match.
Never substitute espeak or a system voice and call it Irina.
Avoid synthetic gaps above 0.22 seconds in short explainer narration unless the script explicitly requires a dramatic pause.
Use soft phrase endings and low-level room tone instead of hard zero-silence edits.
Do not over-compress; preserve a relaxed spoken feel.
Keep speech intelligibility above ambience and SFX.
For short lessons, default to one 5-10 second free sample before any longer render.
